name: Netflix Timed Text Style Guide
value: 2 frames
notes: At 24 fps, gaps of 3-11 frames must be closed to 2 frames; gaps should be either 2 frames or at least half a second (12 frames at 24 fps, 15 at 30 fps, 30 at 60 fps).

name: Netflix Timed Text Style Guide

notes: In-time on the first frame of audio, within 1-2 frames acceptable. Snap to shot changes within half a second, keeping 2 frames before the cut.

name: BBC Subtitle Guidelines
value: 37 fixed-width characters (Teletext), fewer if coloured text is used

name: BBC Subtitle Guidelines
value: 68% of video width for 16:9; 90% for 4:3, 1:1 and 9:16
notes: As a guide, 37 characters in a 75% region of 16:9 equals about 25 characters in a 90% region of 9:16. Content for both platforms must meet both limits.

name: BBC Subtitle Guidelines
value: 2 for 16:9, 4:3 and 1:1; 3 for vertical 9:16
notes: Extra lines allowed only if no important picture information is obscured.

name: BBC Subtitle Guidelines
value: 160-180 words per minute (0.33 to 0.375 s per word); aim for at least about 0.3 s per word on screen
applies_to: BBC pre-recorded subtitles; live subtitle word rate also 160-180 wpm
notes: Children's subtitles should generally follow the speed of speech, with producer advice where that rate is unsuitable for the age group.

name: BBC Subtitle Guidelines
value: If a gap is left: minimum 1 second, preferably 1.5 seconds
notes: Contrasts with Netflix, which chains subtitles with a 2-frame gap.

name: BBC Subtitle Guidelines
value: EBU-TT-D (online only) or EBU-TT 1.0 (broadcast and online); STL file rules documented separately

name: YouTube

notes: SRT and SBV: basic versions only, no styling recognized, file must be plain UTF-8.

value: Binary file format for exchange of teletext and in-vision subtitles between broadcasters
applies_to: Broadcast exchange (legacy, still accepted by YouTube and BBC workflows)

name: EBU subtitle formats
value: XML (TTML-based) archiving and interchange format; current v1.2, May 2017 (v1.0 July 2012)

name: EBU subtitle formats
value: XML (TTML-based) format for distribution over IP; current v1.0.1, May 2018, aligned with W3C IMSC 1.0.1

name: SRT (SubRip)
value: Numeric counter; timing line HH:MM:SS,mmm --> HH:MM:SS,mmm (comma before milliseconds, arrow is two hyphens + '>'); one or more text lines; blank line ends the cue
notes: No formal published specification exists. SubRip software defaulted to Windows-1252 encoding, so parsers must detect charset; YouTube requires plain UTF-8. The LoC description mentions a 32-character line limit, which is not a formal rule and conflicts with platform guides (Netflix 42, BBC 37).

name: WebVTT (W3C)
value: UTF-8 text, MIME type text/vtt; optional BOM then the string 'WEBVTT' on the first line, followed by a blank line; cue = optional identifier, timing line, payload
notes: Optional STYLE, REGION and NOTE blocks; STYLE blocks must come before the first cue.

name: WebVTT (W3C)
value: [hh:]mm:ss.ttt with a full stop before exactly 3 millisecond digits; hours optional unless non-zero; start --> end with spaces
notes: Cue start times must not decrease through the file; end must be greater than start; cues may overlap. Key difference from SRT: '.' instead of ',' and the WEBVTT header.
